exampleRespondent.name: Sarah Williams
exampleRespondent.areaOfExpertise: Rural insurance claims, especially farm property and weather-related damage

sections.title: What problem are you trying to solve?

questions.label: In plain English, what is the issue?
questions.sampleAnswer: Claims handlers spend too much time searching policy documents, internal guidance, previous claim notes, and repair guidance before deciding the next best action.

questions.label: Who is affected by this problem?
questions.sampleAnswer: Claims handlers, team leaders, brokers, and customers waiting for claim decisions.

questions.label: Why does this matter now?
questions.sampleAnswer: Storm-related claims are increasing, and newer handlers need more support to make consistent decisions.

sections.title: What does a good outcome look like?

questions.label: What would success look like for your team?
questions.sampleAnswer: Handlers can quickly understand what guidance applies to a claim, what information is missing, and what they should do next.

questions.label: How would you measure improvement?
What should not happen?
questions.sampleAnswer: The AI should not approve or reject claims by itself. It should support the handler, not replace their judgement.

questions.label: Who are the main users?
questions.sampleAnswer: Claims handlers and claims team leaders.

questions.label: How experienced are they?
questions.sampleAnswer: Mixed experience. Some are senior specialists; others are newer handlers learning rural and agricultural claims.

questions.label: Where do they work today?
questions.sampleAnswer: They work across claims systems, email, Teams, policy documents, internal guidance, and case notes.

sections.title: Where should the agent show up?

questions.label: Where would users naturally expect to use this agent?
At what point in the work should the agent appear?
questions.sampleAnswer: When a handler opens a new rural property claim, reviews incoming evidence, prepares a customer update, or decides whether to escalate the case.

questions.label: Should the agent wait to be asked, or should it proactively alert users?
options: Wait until the user asks for help
Proactively alert users when something important is missing or risky
questions.sampleAnswer: Both, depending on the situation

sections.title: What should the AI help with?

questions.label: What questions should it answer?
sampleAnswer: What policy wording may apply to this claim?
Has this type of claim been handled before?
What guidance should the handler consider?
When should the claim be escalated?

questions.label: What tasks should it help complete?
What should remain human-owned?
questions.sampleAnswer: Claim decisions, approvals, customer commitments, complaint handling, and any payment decision.

questions.label: What business knowledge should the AI use?
Where does this information live today?
questions.sampleAnswer: SharePoint, internal claims systems, email templates, policy PDFs, team guidance notes, and experienced colleagues' knowledge.

questions.label: Is the information always up to date?
questions.sampleAnswer: Not always. Some guidance is formal and current, while some local knowledge sits with senior handlers.

questions.label: What could go wrong if the AI gives poor advice?
questions.sampleAnswer: A handler could give the wrong customer message, miss an escalation point, or apply the wrong policy guidance.

questions.label: What information is sensitive?
sampleAnswer: Commercially sensitive farm or business data

questions.label: What controls would make you comfortable?

sections.title: How should it feel to use?

questions.label: What tone should the AI have?
questions.sampleAnswer: Clear, practical, and careful. It should sound like a helpful senior claims colleague, not a chatbot making decisions.

questions.label: What would make users trust it?
questions.sampleAnswer: It explains its reasoning, links to source guidance, flags uncertainty, and does not pretend to know things it cannot verify.

questions.label: What would make users reject it?
questions.sampleAnswer: Generic answers, overconfidence, wrong policy references, or anything that feels like it is replacing claims expertise.

questions.label: Describe a real-world situation
questions.sampleAnswer: A customer reports storm damage to several outbuildings on a farm. The handler needs to understand what cover may apply, what evidence is needed, whether any exclusions matter, and whether the case should be escalated.

questions.label: What should the AI do in this situation?
questions.sampleAnswer: Summarise the claim, find the relevant policy wording and claims guidance, list missing information, suggest the next handler actions, and draft a careful customer update.

questions.label: What should the AI not do?
questions.sampleAnswer: It should not confirm cover, reject the claim, approve payment, or send the customer message without handler review.

questions.label: If this AI assistant existed tomorrow, what would you most want it to help your team with first?
questions.sampleAnswer: Helping claims handlers find the right guidance quickly and understand the next best action for routine rural property claims.
